name: Animated Line Art. Category: Motion Design and Cinematography. Provenance: supplemental, user-requested direction.
visualIdentity: Subjects are built from contours, connectors, arrows, and paths with consistent widths, caps, and joins. Objects appear before their relationships, then connections are drawn, paths followed, or outlines reorganized. Completed structures stay readable. This is distinct from static line art and from line boil.
suitableUses: Explicitly suggested fits include technical explainers, process diagrams, annual-report motion, and educational lessons. Inferred suitability covers relationship or network diagrams where sequential reveal aids comprehension. Stated use cases are suggestions, and specific client or brief requirements are unspecified.
limitations: Avoid arbitrary tangled lines and endlessly repeated drawing. The style does not establish photorealistic materials or validated physics, and simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production. Sketch or hachure treatments are optional and do not create authentic pencil or ink media. Rough.js does not provide handwriting or character poses.
palette: The palette is an authored, style-compatible suggestion, not canonical: background #F9F4E7, foreground #27434A, accent_1 #AA6945. Task-provided or approved palettes override it, and gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 9.619:1 and meets the 4.5:1 normal-text target. Accent on background measures 3.971:1, so it is decorative only. Recheck composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Paths are revealed with stroke-dasharray, stroke-dashoffset, or DrawSVGPlugin, sequenced by explanatory order across paths, nodes, and arrows. Video motion must derive from seekable composition time. Interactive HTML may bind progress to scroll, but it needs reduced-motion static states. Deliberate cuts and reading holds should be preserved. Easing or springs are optional, not required.
audio: Audio is unspecified because the style mandates no soundtrack. Suggested options include optional background music, voiceover explaining the topic, restrained sound accents on key reveals, and silence during reading holds. User-specified audio takes priority. Audio should not compete with narration. Speech intelligibility, balance, and picture sync must be verified in the final video.
assetRequirements: No source assets were supplied, so asset needs are unspecified. Likely inputs are diagram structure or subject geometry, exact copy, and any approved palette. Optional inputs include tldraw-exported SVG layers, cached graph positions, and seeded Rough.js geometry. Audio must be authorized. Motion references motion-012 and motion-015 are optional and need scene screening; choosing none is valid.
combinations: Documented suggestions include style-001, a Swiss grid with flush-left labels that keeps strokes grid-aligned, suited to technical explainers. Style-024 adds handwritten annotations for lessons, appearing only after the structure is readable, with at most one note per idea. Avoid heavy color fields and mixing looser annotation strokes into structural lines. Suitability of these pairings is inferred.
productionApproach: Suggested visual renderer is native SVG, with Cytoscape.js, Paper.js, or p5.js only where graph or geometry needs justify them. Suggested motion engine is GSAP DrawSVGPlugin, with Anime.js or Motion optional and one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline using a paused, seekable GSAP timeline in window.__timelines. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Validate with hyperframes check and snapshot, then render and inspect decoded frames and audio sync. These are suggested routes, not the source's actual toolchain.
